title: Runs of a phase-hosted machine
statement: Let $k$ be a natural number, let $\Gamma$ and $I$ be types, let $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ be a state type for each $i\in I$, let $M_i$ be a $k$-work-tape machine with state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$, and let $q_0$ be a state tagged by an element of $I$. Suppose $c,c'$ are configurations of $M_i$ on input $x$, $T\in\mathbb{N}$, and running $M_i$ from $c$ for $T$ steps yields $c'$. If $s'$ is the state of $c'$ and the reduction rule sends $(i,s')$ to $q'$, and if at every time $u<T$ the run of $M_i$ from $c$ is in a state $s$ for which the reduction rule sends $(i,s)$ to no state, then for every $u\le T$ the phase-hosted machine's run from the configuration $c$ tagged by $i$ agrees with the run of $M_i$ from $c$ tagged by $i$, and after $T+1$ steps it is $c'$ with its state replaced by $q'$.
hypotheses_covered: $k\in\mathbb{N}$; symbol alphabet $\Gamma$ and phase index type $I$
A phase state type $\mathrm{Ph}(i)$ and machine $M_i$ for every $i\in I$
An initial tagged state $q_0$ and reduction rule on phase states
